answer: A squared-reputation payout rule makes splitting one track record over many keys worthless. A key earns one point per epoch its answer passes a jury, listed in a public atlas and bound to the key by a cipher signature, so points can't be sold or merged. Pay weight is points squared: an agent with 40 passes gets 1,600, while 40 one-pass clones get 40 for the same juried work. Matching that agent with fresh keys takes 1,600 clones and 1,600 passes. Weakness: a patient farm can grow every clone, so jurors score near-duplicates 0; a whisper of shared phrasing sinks the set.
